title: Table shuffleboard: slide the weight down a 9-ft board with one push so it stops in the 3-point zone
instruction: Slide the red-capped weight down the shuffleboard with one push so that it stops in the 3-point zone at the far end: completely past the 3-line, 6 inches from the end, without falling off. Keep it on the board: slide it, do not throw it, and do not touch it again once it has left your hand.
context: Table shuffleboard is a fixture of bars, clubs and game rooms; the 9-ft size is sold for apartments and small bars. On a waxed board the weight's travel grows with the square of its speed, so stopping in a 6-inch zone 2 m away needs one clean release at the right speed, flat and straight, with no chance to correct it.
setup: A 9-ft table shuffleboard (as in Champion's 9-ft championship table): a waxed maple playfield 7 ft 8 in x 20 in (2.337 x 0.508 m), its top 30 in (0.762 m) above the floor, running straight ahead of the robot from x = 0.280 m to 2.617 m, centred on y = -0.305 m. It sits in an oak cradle 31 in wide and 9 ft long with gutters 65 mm below the board (100 mm wide at the sides, 200 mm long at each end); the cradle's near end is 5 mm in front of the robot's pedestals. Painted lines 6 mm wide: one foul line across the middle (1.448 m), and at each end the 3-line 6 in and the 2-line 12 in from the end (far end: 2.465 m and 2.312 m); the far zones carry 3, 2 and 1 red dots. One weight (as in McClure's 2 5/16 in weights with plastic caps): a chrome-plated steel puck 2 5/16 in (58.7 mm) across and 0.75 in high with a red plastic cap 55 mm across and 13 mm high, 345 g in all, standing on the board's centre line at x = 0.315 m, 35 mm from the near end. Two YAM arms on 750 mm pedestals at x = 0, y = +/-0.305 m (the right arm straight behind the weight), 40 N parallel grippers.
scoring: The trial scores 0 if the weight is ever more than 5 mm above the board with nothing touching it (thrown), if the robot touches it after it has left the hand sliding at 0.1 m/s or more, if it leaves the board after the shot (into a gutter), or if the table moves. Otherwise the score is set by where the weight comes to rest after the shot, flat (under 10 degrees), untouched and still (under 5 mm/s for 1 s); as in the game, a weight touching a line counts the lower zone: 1.0 completely past the 3-line (6 in from the far end), including a weight hanging over the end; 0.5 completely past the 2-line (12 in from the end); 0.25 completely past the foul line in the middle; 0 short of it.
reset_notes: Stand the weight back on the centre line 35 mm from the near end and brush the playfield smooth. Before each set of trials, check the board's speed: push a weight down it by hand and film it at 60 fps beside a tape measure on the board. Read its speed from its positions 1 s apart: it must slow by 0.18 to 0.22 m/s each second (friction 0.02). Sprinkle on silicone shuffleboard wax to make the board faster, or wipe some off to make it slower, and check again.
fidelity: PhysX at 960 Hz, 20 Hz control. Sizes and mass from tournament rules and makers' specifications. The waxed board is a uniform friction of 0.02 (a fast board; published examples range from 0.012 to 0.08), not loose silicone beads; the board is perfectly flat, the puck a straight cylinder without its slight taper, no air drag, unpadded gutters. Unmodified YAM arms, 40 N grippers.
